summary: ETHOnline 2026 is an ETHGlobal online hackathon with sponsor prize pools from The Graph ($15,000), Hedera ($15,000), Arc ($10,000), World ($7,000), 1inch ($7,000), ENS ($5,000), Uniswap Foundation ($5,000), Ledger ($5,000), Privy ($5,000), Chainlink ($3,000), and Bazantic ($3,000). Tracks cover composable blockchain data, agentic payments, stablecoin DeFi, identity, tokenization, confidential workflows, and AI tooling, including separate awards for net-new builds and Continuity Track work on existing projects. Most tracks require a live integration rather than mocks, plus a public repository and a demo; part of each Arc prize is paid only if the same project is deployed to Arc Mainnet by September 30.

deadlines.name: Arc Mainnet deployment for conditional prize portion
deadlines.notes: Year is not stated. For Best DeFi/Onchain Finance Application and Best Agentic Economy Application with Circle Agent Stack, $2,500 of each $3,500 is awarded only if the same project is deployed to Arc Mainnet by September 30. For Best DeFi or Agentic Application (Continuity), $2,000 of the $3,000 is awarded only if deployed to Arc Mainnet by September 30.

deadlines.name: Chainlink Automated Liquidation Protection Challenge join window
deadlines.notes: Call join() on the Ethereum Sepolia challenge contract from Sept 9 until the hackathon submission deadline. A calendar date for the submission deadline is not stated.

deadlines.name: Hackathon submission deadline
deadlines.notes: Referenced as the cutoff for joining the Chainlink challenge and for freezing liquidation-protection workflows. No calendar date is stated in the brief.

deadlines.name: Chainlink challenge scenario run

tracks.name: Best Use of Composable or Standardized Graph Products
requirements: Build on The Graph's composable and standardized data products: use Standardized Subgraphs to query many protocols of a type, compose reusable Substreams packages, layer Subgraph MCP for cross-protocol analysis, or contribute a new composable Substreams module for an emerging standard such as ERC-4626 tokenized-vault flows.
Either compose two or more of The Graph's products, or build meaningfully on a standardized schema (for example the Messari Standardized Subgraphs).
Consume live data from a Graph provider, for example Subgraph Studio for Subgraphs or The Graph Market for Substreams. Mocked, local-only, or static datasets do not qualify.
Simply querying one Subgraph with no composition or standardization does not qualify.
Authoring or extending a Standardized Subgraph, or contributing a reusable composable Substreams module, is in scope.
Make the standards leverage clear: show what became easier because a shared schema or composed product was used.
Submit a public repository and a short demo video (two to four minutes).

tracks.name: Best AI Tooling or AI Use Case with The Graph (From Scratch)
requirements: This is the From Scratch / Start Fresh pool: projects begun and built during the hackathon. Open-source starter kits are fine; project-specific prior code is not.

Use The Graph as a load-bearing part of the project: AI tooling must target The Graph's products or AI Suite, or the agent/app must use Subgraphs, the Subgraph MCP, or Substreams as its source of blockchain data.

Rewards tooling that makes The Graph easier to use from AI environments such as Claude, Cursor, and ChatGPT (new or extended MCP servers, agent SKILLs, x402 payment tooling, A2A integrations, framework plugins, or client configs) and AI agents or apps that use The Graph as live blockchain data.

Consume live data from a Graph provider, for example querying Subgraphs with an API key from Subgraph Studio, or streaming Substreams via The Graph Market. Mocked, local-only, or static datasets do not qualify.

Do meaningful work with the data: reasoning, decisions, automation, or a natural-language interface, not just printing a raw query result. Tooling submissions must be reusable infrastructure, not a single end-user app.
Open-source the code with a clear README or SKILL.md so judges can run it, and submit a public repository plus a short demo video (two to four minutes).
Select the Start Fresh pool and follow that pool's ETHGlobal rules.
For the featured Substreams one-prompt deployment challenge: demonstrate deploying a working Substreams pipeline from a single prompt using the Substreams SKILLs.

tracks.name: Best AI Tooling or AI Use Case with The Graph (Continuity)
requirements: This prize is only available to Continuity Track participants.

Continuity means extending an existing open-source repo or shipping a new feature on an existing product. Document the pre-existing work; only work done during the event is judged. Extending The Graph's own AI Suite (for example improving an existing MCP server or SKILL) fits this pool.

Use The Graph as a load-bearing part of the project: AI tooling must target The Graph's products or AI Suite, or the agent/app must use Subgraphs, the Subgraph MCP, or Substreams as its source of blockchain data.

Consume live data from a Graph provider, for example querying Subgraphs with an API key from Subgraph Studio, or streaming Substreams via The Graph Market. Mocked, local-only, or static datasets do not qualify.

Do meaningful work with the data: reasoning, decisions, automation, or a natural-language interface, not just printing a raw query result. Tooling submissions must be reusable infrastructure, not a single end-user app.
Open-source the code with a clear README or SKILL.md so judges can run it, and submit a public repository plus a short demo video (two to four minutes).
Select the Continuity pool, follow that pool's ETHGlobal rules, and document any pre-existing work.
For the featured Substreams one-prompt deployment challenge: demonstrate deploying a working Substreams pipeline from a single prompt using the Substreams SKILLs.

tracks.name: AI & Agentic Payments on Hedera
requirements: Stand up a real x402-gated service on Hedera and build the platform that consumes it.

tracks.name: Open Source — Improve the Hedera Harness

tracks.name: Tokenization of Anything

Use the Asset Tokenization Studio (SDK, contracts, web application, or a combination) to issue or manage a tokenised asset.
Deploy and demonstrate on Hedera testnet.
Public GitHub repo, with contracts verified on HashScan where applicable.
Demo video of five minutes or less showing issuance, configuration, and at least one lifecycle operation such as a transfer, compliance check, or distribution.

tracks.name: Built on Hedera
requirements: This prize is only available to Continuity Track participants.

Demonstrate substantive new work completed during this event: new features, new Hedera services integrated, or a significant architectural change. Polish and bug fixes alone will not qualify.
Public GitHub repo with a README that clearly separates what existed before from what is new, ideally with commit history or a diff.
Demo video of five minutes or less focused on the new work.

tracks.name: AI Agents x Ledger
requirements: Start something new during the event. Device-backed security must be central: agents that hold secrets they cannot leak, agents that pay for what they use, systems that ask for a human before anything irreversible, or products that make autonomous behavior safer instead of bypassing user intent.

Agents that use secrets they cannot leak (a broker hands out scoped capabilities, never the API key) and bringing the Key Ring to hosts with no USB port (enroll a VPS, a CI runner, or a hosted agent) must both be built on the Ledger Agent Stack, and in particular on the Ledger Key Ring CLI (wallet-cli ring).

Also sought: agents that pay for APIs, tools, or services with Ledger-secured payment flows, including x402-style patterns, and human-in-the-loop agents where Ledger approves high-risk actions before funds move or permissions escalate.

tracks.name: Extend to Ledger
requirements: This prize is only available to Continuity Track participants.
For teams extending a project they already had before the event. Show what the Ledger Agent Stack adds to something real.

Example directions stated in the brief: add a Ledger signer to an already shipped app using the DMK skills; make wallet-cli ring the key backend for existing .env, sops, or age files; put a device confirmation in front of an action the product already performs; or pick up an open issue on a Ledger repository and land it as a real fix.

tracks.name: Best B2B financial product
requirements: Build a product that helps businesses manage digital assets and financial operations with Privy, such as treasury platforms, business accounts, payroll, spend management, payment operations, or shared organization wallets.
Integrate Privy as a core part of the product.
Create or use at least one Privy wallet.
Demonstrate a business or organization use case.
Implement at least one functional B2B workflow, such as a payment, approval, treasury operation, or wallet administration flow.
Use at least one Privy control, such as policies, signers, key quorums, or intents.
Provide a working demo and access to the project's source code.
Clearly explain how Privy enables the product.

tracks.name: Best financial flow
requirements: Build a seamless experience for funding, moving, trading, growing, or spending digital assets with Privy.
Integrate Privy as a core part of the product.
Create or use at least one Privy wallet.

Complete at least one functional financial flow using a generally available Privy feature. Eligible flows include transfers, bridging, stablecoin conversions, swaps, self-service Earn vaults, onramps, or other supported wallet actions.
Provide a working demo and access to the project's source code.
Clearly explain how Privy improves the user experience.
Features requiring commercial or guided onboarding may be mocked, but they do not count as the required functional Privy integration.
Privy Cards currently requires guided Privy and Bridge onboarding; a mocked card experience is allowed only if another live Privy flow is included for eligibility.

tracks.name: Best Confidential Workflow
requirements: Build a privacy-preserving Web3 application with Chainlink Runtime Environment (CRE) Confidential Workflows.
Build a CRE Workflow that uses Confidential Workflows to execute a meaningful part of the application.
The workflow must register and use a confidential TEE handler, such as handlerInTee in TypeScript or cre.HandlerInTee in Go.
The confidential portion must process at least one sensitive input, secret, confidential API response, private parameter, or intermediate value inside the enclave.
The Confidential Workflow must be meaningfully integrated into the project's core functionality. A placeholder handler or isolated example does not qualify.
Demonstrate a successful execution through a Confidential Workflow simulation using the CRE CLI or a live deployment on the CRE network.
Provide evidence of the successful simulation or deployment, such as a demo video, terminal output, execution logs, or deployment details.

tracks.name: Best Chainlink-Powered Upgrade
requirements: This prize is only available to Continuity Track participants.
Build a meaningful upgrade to an existing project, protocol, or infrastructure using Chainlink technology.
Integrate at least one Chainlink service directly within smart contract logic or onchain workflows.
The Chainlink integration must contribute to a state change on a blockchain. Simply displaying Chainlink data in a frontend is not sufficient.
The submission must clearly demonstrate how the Chainlink-powered upgrade improves the existing project.
Use CRE instead of Chainlink Functions or Automation. Functions and Automation are being deprecated.
Eligible technologies: CRE including Confidential Workflows, Price Feeds, Data Streams, Proof of Reserve, and VRF.

tracks.name: Automated Liquidation Protection Challenge
requirements: Build a Confidential Workflow that protects a virtual ETH-collateral/USDC-debt position during simulated market movements.
The workflow must avoid liquidation, preserve the benefit of keeping the loan open, use emergency capital efficiently, and keep sensitive protection rules and credentials private.

Until the hackathon submission deadline, update the workflow to join the official challenge using join() on the Ethereum Sepolia challenge contract 0x88574e7Cc0027afd04951daa09B64d4441931ba1, from Sept 9 to the hackathon submission deadline.
You cannot update the workflow after the hackathon submission deadline.
After the deadline, the Chainlink team will run the scenarios during the next 24h and discover the winner.

tracks.name: Help an Agent Use Your Hackathon Project
requirements: This prize is only available to Continuity Track participants.
Show an agent can use the project without the builder explaining it, using a Bazantic-built MCP server and recipe.
Create an account on bazantic.com.
Create an x402/MPP Gateway in Bazantic for the project.
Create a Recipe that explains when, why, and how to use the service.
Use the same prompt, model, settings, and API access in both tests. Make the Recipe the only material difference between a raw-API test and a Recipe test.
Show both results and identify the improvement by sharing the inputs and results in the submission.
Record a video walking through the difference in outcomes.
Provide the Bazantic account username (email or GitHub handle) so the recipe can be attributed.

tracks.name: Best Recipe that uses EthGlobal Hackathon Sponsor APIs
requirements: Create a set of recipes that use multiple APIs the project utilizes, forming a repeatable workflow that moves from one service to the next and completes a task neither could solve alone.
Create an account on bazantic.com.
Create an x402/MPP Gateway in Bazantic for the project.
Use at least one other service already available through Bazantic OR available from a sponsor of the EthGlobal Online Hackathon.
Create a recipe that uses both services in one working flow.
Make the final result depend meaningfully on both services.
Demonstrate the completed task from start to finish in a screen recording that is part of the submission.
Provide the Bazantic account username (email or GitHub handle).

tracks.name: Agentify a new API
requirements: Add a new API into Bazantic and create a recipe, connected with the hackathon project, demonstrating something agents could not do before.
Create an account on bazantic.com.
Create an x402/MPP Gateway in Bazantic for the project.
Add a service that was not available through Bazantic AND is not an API available via the other sponsors when the event began.
Create a working Gateway for that service on Bazantic.
Create a recipe that uses both services in one working flow within the hackathon project.
Explain how other builders and agents could use the new service by demonstrating what the recipe does in a screen recording.
Provide the Bazantic account username (email or GitHub handle).

judging_criteria.name: 1inch SwapVM utilization
judging_criteria.description: On both Aqua tracks, projects that utilize SwapVM will be scored higher during final judging.

judging_criteria.name: ENS AI agent bonus
judging_criteria.description: Best Use of ENSv2: bonus points for bringing AI agents into the mix, such as agents as namespaces with their own identity and permissions. The integration track also says it pairs well with AI agent identity.

judging_criteria.name: Hedera agentic payments extra points
judging_criteria.description: Extra points for pay-per-call inference, data, or compute metering rather than a flat per-request charge; multi-agent negotiation and settlement via A2A or ACP; on-chain agent identity using ERC-8004 or HCS-14; agent discovery via UCP or a directory; HTS tokens or custom fee schedules; verifiable payment audit trails on HCS; recurring or streamed payments using Scheduled Transactions.

judging_criteria.name: Hedera Harness extra points
judging_criteria.description: Extra points for new service coverage, better ergonomics, or fewer lines of code to a working transaction; tests, documentation, or examples; a harness targeting a language or framework the current one does not cover; clear before-and-after evidence of a developer-experience gain.

judging_criteria.name: Hedera tokenization extra points
judging_criteria.description: Real asset classes and real lifecycle management are favoured over a token with a name on it. Extra points for a secondary market for ATS-issued assets, compliance controls (KYC grants, freezes, transfer restrictions, pauses), custom fee schedules, coupon or dividend distributions, royalty flows, oracle integration for pricing or NAV, Scheduled Transactions for vesting, coupons, or maturity, and contributions upstream to ATS.

judging_criteria.name: Built on Hedera extra points
judging_criteria.description: Extra points for evidence of real users, traction, or deployment beyond the demo; newly integrated Hedera services that were not in the original build; and a clear roadmap for what comes after the hackathon.

judging_criteria.name: Arc DeFi what they are looking for
judging_criteria.description: Meaningful use of Arc and USDC; advanced programmable money flows such as conditional payments, onchain automation, or multi-step settlement; payment, liquidity, or treasury workflows using App Kits where relevant; applications that show why stablecoin-native infrastructure changes what is possible.

judging_criteria.name: Arc agentic what they are looking for
judging_criteria.description: Agents with clear decision logic tied to real signals; autonomous spending, payments, or settlement flows using USDC; use of Agent Stack to connect agents to wallets, USDC payments, and onchain actions; use of Nanopayments, Paymaster, or App Kits where relevant for agent-to-agent or service payments.

judging_criteria.name: Chainlink liquidation challenge outcome
judging_criteria.description: After the submission deadline, the Chainlink team runs scenarios for the next 24 hours and discovers the winner. The workflow must avoid liquidation, preserve the benefit of keeping the loan open, use emergency capital efficiently, and keep sensitive protection rules and credentials private. No numeric weights are stated.

rules: Prizes marked only for Continuity Track participants are: The Graph AI Continuity, Hedera Built on Hedera, Arc Best DeFi or Agentic Application, World AgentKit Continuity, 1inch Build an Aqua App - Continuity Track, ENS Best Integration of ENSv2 into an Existing Project, the $2,000 Uniswap Foundation Best Uniswap Stack Contribution, Ledger Extend to Ledger, Chainlink Best Chainlink-Powered Upgrade, and Bazantic Help an Agent Use Your Hackathon Project.

The Graph AI prize is judged in two pools. Start Fresh: projects begun and built during the hackathon; open-source starter kits are fine; project-specific prior code is not. Continuity: extend an existing open-source repo or ship a new feature on an existing product; document pre-existing work; only work done during the event is judged.
Where the brief says to follow a pool's ETHGlobal rules, those rules are not restated in this prize page.
Mocked, local-only, or static datasets do not qualify for The Graph prizes. Live data from a Graph provider is required.
Simply querying one Subgraph with no composition or standardization does not qualify for the composable/standardized Graph prize.
Hedera Built on Hedera: the project must already exist on Hedera or have been built for a previous hackathon. Polish and bug fixes alone do not qualify.

Arc: part of each prize is awarded only if the same project is deployed to Arc Mainnet by September 30 ($2,500 of $3,500 on the two non-continuity tracks; $2,000 of $3,000 on the Continuity track). Submissions must state which Arc bounty they are for.
ENSv2 prizes require ENSv2 on Sepolia, a functional demo that is not hard-coded values, and open-source code. The integration prize must target an existing project's testnet deployment.

1inch: official Aqua/SwapVM contracts must be used; redeployments of a modified SwapVM contract are allowed. Proper Git commit history is required; single-commit entries on the final day do not qualify.
Uniswap submissions without FEEDBACK.md and a completed Uniswap Developer Feedback Form will be reviewed and audited before winners are finalized.

Privy features requiring commercial or guided onboarding may be mocked, but they do not count as the required functional Privy integration. A mocked Privy Cards experience is allowed only with another live Privy flow.
Chainlink Functions and Automation are being deprecated. Projects needing that functionality should implement it using CRE.
Chainlink liquidation-protection workflows cannot be updated after the hackathon submission deadline. The Chainlink team runs scenarios during the following 24 hours.
Bazantic Agentify a new API: the added service must not already be available through Bazantic and must not be an API available via the other sponsors when the event began.
No overall eligibility rules, team-size limits, or a calendar date for the hackathon submission deadline are stated on this prize page.
